heading: As told by the Founder
text:
I, Hellen Nyilak, was born and raised deep in the village, where life was hard enough that we sometimes had nothing to eat. The nearest school was at least five miles away, and with no means of transport, we walked there on foot — often missing class altogether when the rains made the roads impassable.

My parents could not afford my school fees, so they paid in cassava and maize instead. I sold mangoes and firewood, and worked in other people's gardens, just to raise enough money for my own school fees and help support my siblings.

I grew up hearing the elders say "somu ber" — education is good — and I made myself a promise: when I grew up, I would open a school for every child whose family could not afford to pay fees.

In 2022, I kept that promise. Biggi Junior School opened its doors in Marama Lower (now Ndaba Village), Marama Parish, Panyimur Sub-County, Jonam County, Pakwach District. Guided by our motto, "Education for a Brighter Future," we set out to make sure every family in this community could send their children to school — believing that education today means a better future for everyone, here and beyond.

Most families in this area once depended on fishing on Lake Albert. Since the government's fishing ban on this part of the lake, combined with the region's hot, dry climate, many have been left with almost no way to earn a living.

Alongside our academic curriculum, we equip our pupils with practical skills — including book-making, cookery, and soap-making — to give them tools for the future, whatever path they choose.

I invite you to join us. Lend a hand, support a child, and help build a brighter future for this community.
